Prompt Highlighting in Large Language Models

Lingrui Mei1Jiayu Yao1Jiafeng Guo1Xueqi Cheng1

Abstract
Prompt highlighting steers a large language model to prioritize user-specified text
spans during generation. A key challenge is extracting steering directions that
capture the difference between relevant and irrelevant contexts, rather than shared
structural patterns common to both. We propose PRISM- ∆(Projection-based
Relevance-InformedSteeringMethod), which decomposes the difference between
positive and negative cross-covariance matrices to maximize discriminative energy
while eliminating shared directions. Each attention head receives a continuous
softplus importance weight, letting weak-but-useful heads contribute at reduced
strength. The framework extends naturally to Value representations, capturing
content-channel signal that Key-only methods leave unused. Across four bench-
marks and five models, PRISM- ∆matches or exceeds the best existing method on
19 of 20 configurations, with relative gains up to +10.6%, while halving the fluency
cost of steering. PRISM- ∆also scales to long-context retrieval, outperforming the
best existing method by up to +4.8% relative gain. PRISM- ∆is compatible with
FlashAttention and adds negligible memory overhead.
1 Introduction
Large language models frequently need to prioritize specific parts of their input. When presented with
conflicting information, the model should attend to newly provided facts over its parametric memory.
In long-context retrieval, the answer may reside in the middle of thirty passages, where models
notoriously underperform [Liu et al., 2024]. This problem is known asprompt highlighting[Li et al.,
2026]: given a prompt and a marked subset of tokens, the goal is to amplify the model’s attention to
those tokens so that generation becomes more accurate and faithful to user intent.
Several prompt highlighting methods have been proposed, including post-hoc attention score ma-
nipulation [Zhang et al., 2023], logit-level anchoring [Tian and Zhang, 2024], and pre-attention Key
vector editing via spectral decomposition [Li et al., 2026]. However, all of them operate solely on
therouting channel—Key representations that control where the model looks. Transformer attention
output also depends on acontent channel—Value representations that determine what information is
transmitted. Even when routing successfully directs the model to attend to highlighted tokens, the
information those tokens convey through their Value representations remains unenhanced.
We investigate whether the Value channel carries useful signal by extracting Key and Value represen-
tations under contrastive conditions. Value shifts are comparable in magnitude to Key across all five

We propose PRISM- ∆(Projection-basedRelevance-InformedSteeringMethod), which steers both
channels through discriminative subspace learning and adaptive head weighting (Figure 1). Our
contributions are:
•We introducedifferential cross-covariance decompositionto extract maximally discrimina-
tive directions from contrastive data. Each head’s signal strength is mapped to a continuous
softplus weight, enabling adaptive steering that suppresses noisy heads while preserving
weak-but-useful ones.
•We extend this framework tojointly steer Key and Value channels. The Value channel
reduces the fluency degradation caused by steering and improves generation consistency.
PRISM- ∆consistently outperforms the best existing method on three short-context benchmarks
across five models, with relative gains up to +10.6%, and further scales to long-context retrieval with
up to +4.8% gain on 30-passage inputs.
2 Related work
Prompt highlighting.PASTA [Zhang et al., 2023] modifies attention scores post-hoc but is in-
compatible with FlashAttention [Dao et al., 2022]. SPA [Tian and Zhang, 2024] anchors at the
logit level but requires multiple forward passes. SEKA [Li et al., 2026] edits Key vectors via spec-
tral decomposition with near-zero overhead. All three operate exclusively on the routing channel,
leaving the content channel unused. PRISM- ∆differs by jointly steering Key and Value channels
with per-head continuous weighting, capturing both routing and content gains. Prefix-Tuning [Li
and Liang, 2021] also operates in Key/Value space by prepending learned soft tokens, but requires
gradient-based training and modifies the context length; PRISM- ∆is gradient-free and edits existing
token representations in place.
Activation editing and head specialization.SEA [Qiu et al., 2024], Representation Engineer-
ing [Zou et al., 2023], Inference-Time Intervention [Li et al., 2023], Activation Addition [Turner
et al., 2024], instruction-following steering [Stolfo et al., 2024], and CARVE [Ge et al., 2025] modify
residual stream or attention activations via contrastive signals but do not distinguish Key and Value
roles. Subramani et al. [2022] extract latent steering vectors from pretrained models. In knowledge
editing, ROME [Meng et al., 2022], AlphaEdit [Fang et al., 2025], and Hernandez et al. [2023] target
factual associations through activation or parameter updates. Clark et al. [2019], V oita et al. [2019],
Michel et al. [2019], Elhage et al. [2021], and Olsson et al. [2022] demonstrate that attention heads
exhibit functional specialization, while Wu et al. [2025] identify retrieval heads critical for long-
context factuality. Per-head importance weighting, rather than uniform steering, is therefore better
grounded. PRISM- ∆uses differential SVD to extract per-head discriminative directions and softplus
to assign continuous importance weights; a detailed comparison appears in Table 7 (Appendix B).

4 Experimental setup
Benchmarks.We evaluate on three prompt highlighting benchmarks:BiasBios[De-Arteaga et al.,
2019] (occupation prediction from highlighted biographies; metrics: Accuracy, Fluency, Consistency),
CounterFact[Meng et al., 2022] (knowledge conflict resolution; metrics: Efficacy, Paraphrase), and
Pronoun Change[Li et al., 2026] (rewriting gendered pronouns to gender-neutral forms according
to highlighted instructions; metrics: P. Score measures whether the target pronoun was changed, All-
changed P. Score requires all pronouns to be changed). Formal metric definitions are in Appendix E;
hyperparameters are tuned on held-out validation sets.
Models.We evaluate across two architecture families and three scales: QWEN3-4B/8B/14B-
Base [Yang et al., 2025] and GEMMA3-4B/12B-PT [Gemma Team, 2025].
Baselines.We compare against five baselines:Original(no steering),**-marked(surrounding
highlighted text with asterisks),PASTA[Zhang et al., 2023],SPA[Tian and Zhang, 2024], and
SEKA[Li et al., 2026]. A comparison with AdaSEKA, a higher-cost multi-expert variant, is provided
in Appendix F.
PRISM- ∆configurations.PRISM- ∆uses Key-only steering ( gV= 0). PRISM- ∆V steers both
Key and Value ( gV>0). Projections are constructed offline from 100 synthetic contrastive QA pairs.
Hyperparameters are listed in Appendix G. All experiments use greedy decoding on single NVIDIA
H20 GPUs. Full setup details are in Appendix H.

5.2 Ablation study
Table 2 uses a 2×2 factorial design. Removing softplus costs 0.96% and removing differential
projection costs 0.86% on QWEN3-4B. The interaction is strongly super-additive: from the −Both
baseline, differential projection alone yields −0.02% while softplus alone yields +0.08%, yet their
combination yields +0.94%. This coupling is expected—differential decomposition admits more
heads by lowering the effective threshold, and softplus is needed to down-weight the noisy ones among
them. At matched δmin=0.08 , PRISM- ∆achieves its best result while SEKA drops by 1.36%, because
softplus smoothly down-weights noisy heads rather than giving all activated heads equal weight.
PRISM- ∆-V alone reaches 82.44%, confirming that the Value channel carries independently useful
discriminative signal. A CounterFact ablation (Appendix M), data quantity ablation (Appendix N),
and projection rank analysis (Appendix O) corroborate these findings.

5.4 Efficiency analysis
As shown in Table 4, SEKA adds negligible overhead (+0.01 s, +0.04 GB) over the original model.
PRISM- ∆adds +0.30 s latency (1.26 ×) due to the per-head softplus weight computation and weighted
projection, with negligible additional memory (+0.02 GB). PRISM- ∆V adds a further +0.02 s for
Value editing. Both variants remain fully compatible with FlashAttention [Dao et al., 2022, Dao,
2023]. For comparison, PASTA adds +1.03 s and +23.12 GB, and SPA adds +5.32 s [Li et al., 2026],
placing PRISM-∆in between SEKA and these heavier alternatives.

6.2 Dual-channel contribution decomposition
Table 5 reveals that the Key channel primarily drives accuracy (+12.58% over Vanilla), while the
Value channel preserves generation quality. PRISM- ∆incurs only 53% of SEKA’s fluency cost. Both
PRISM-∆and PRISM-∆V simultaneously outperform SEKA on all three metrics.
Layer-wise signal complementarity.Figure 2b shows that the two channels have complementary
depth profiles. Key signal averages 0.175 in middle layers and Value averages 0.307 in late layers,
with Value surpassing Key from L28 onward. Key directs attention in middle layers while Value
enriches transmitted information in late layers—a functional division rather than redundancy. On
Pronoun Change with GEMMA3-4B, PRISM- ∆V outperforms PRISM- ∆by 1.08%, confirming that
dual-channel steering can surpass Key-only steering on accuracy as well.
6.3 Head selection robustness
Figure 6a sweeps δminfrom 0.06 to 0.20. SEKA drops by 3.14% from its optimum when δmin
is reduced from 0.12 to 0.06: hard thresholding gives all activated heads equal weight w=1 , so
including noisy heads degrades performance. PRISM- ∆fluctuates by only 0.60% across the same
range, because softplus automatically assigns lower weights to less discriminative heads. This
robustness substantially reduces tuning cost (full sweeps over gK,δmin, and γare in Appendix Q).
Figure 6b plots per-sample target log-probabilities: the majority of samples cluster in the upper-right
(both correct) or lower-left (both wrong), while off-diagonal points reveal where the methods diverge.
PRISM- ∆rescues 154 samples that SEKA misclassifies (blue, above diagonal) while losing only 81
(red, below), for a net gain of +73. The 2:1 asymmetry reflects systematic correction of shared-feature
confusion, consistent with the shared-direction elimination of Proposition 1(b). Qualitative examples
are in Appendix R.
7 Conclusion
We presented PRISM- ∆, which steers both the routing and content channels of Transformer attention
for prompt highlighting using differential cross-covariance decomposition and softplus head weight-
ing. Key steering dominates accuracy gains while Value steering reduces fluency degradation. The
complementary depth profiles of Key and Value signals suggest a functional division that may be
useful for other token-level attention interventions and informs future steering research.
Limitations
The main practical limitation is that the optimal gain gKvaries across benchmarks and models,
requiring a validation sweep (typically 5–8 values). On Gemma3 models, optimal hyperparameters
diverge more from Qwen3 defaults, and GEMMA3-12B on Pronoun Change requires a negative gain—
a pattern shared with SEKA [Li et al., 2026], reflecting that the sign of gKdepends on whether the
model’s default tendency aligns with the learned contrastive direction. On near-saturated benchmarks
like CounterFact, absolute gains are inherently small for all steering methods. Prompt highlighting
gives users control over which input spans the model prioritizes. Misuse risks (e.g., amplifying
misleading spans) can be mitigated by restricting highlighting to system-level prompts.

structure.title: Introduction
structure.summary:
The partial document introduces PRISM-∆, a novel method for prompt highlighting in large language models. The core problem addressed is how to effectively steer LLMs to prioritize specific text spans in their input, especially in challenging scenarios like long-context retrieval where models often underperform.

The main points covered are:

*   **Prompt Highlighting:** The goal is to amplify the model's attention to user-specified tokens to improve generation accuracy and faithfulness to user intent.
*   **Limitations of Existing Methods:** Current prompt highlighting techniques primarily focus on manipulating the "routing channel" (Key representations) and neglect the "content channel" (Value representations), leaving potentially useful signals unused.
*   **PRISM-∆'s Approach:** PRISM-∆ proposes a dual-channel steering method that jointly optimizes both Key and Value representations.
*   **Key Innovations:**
    *   **Differential Cross-Covariance Decomposition:** This technique is used to extract maximally discriminative directions by analyzing the differences between positive and negative contexts, while eliminating shared patterns.
    *   **Adaptive Head Weighting:** Each attention head receives a continuous softplus importance weight, allowing for nuanced steering that suppresses noisy heads and preserves weaker but useful ones.
    *   **Joint Steering of Key and Value Channels:** By enhancing both channels, PRISM-∆ aims to reduce fluency degradation and improve generation consistency.
*   **Performance and Scalability:** PRISM-∆ demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods across multiple benchmarks and models, showing relative gains up to +10.6% in short-context tasks and +4.8% in long-context retrieval.
*   **Efficiency and Compatibility:** The method is compatible with FlashAttention and adds negligible memory overhead.
*   **Contrastive Extraction and Dual-Channel Inference:** The document outlines the process of extracting Key and Value representations under different prompting conditions and steering both channels during inference.

This document introduces PRISM-∆, a novel method for prompt highlighting in large language models. Prompt highlighting aims to guide LLMs to prioritize specific text segments during generation. The core challenge addressed is effectively extracting "steering directions" that differentiate relevant from irrelevant context, rather than just common structural patterns.

*   **Differential Subspace Steering:** It decomposes the difference between positive and negative cross-covariance matrices to maximize discriminative energy and eliminate shared directions. This allows it to learn steering directions that are truly informative for highlighting.
*   **Dual-Channel Steering:** Unlike previous methods that focus solely on the "Key" representations (which control where the model looks), PRISM-∆ also steers the "Value" representations (which determine what information is transmitted). This dual-channel approach captures more signal and reduces the fluency cost associated with steering.
*   **Adaptive Head Weighting:** Each attention head receives a continuous softplus importance weight, allowing weaker but still useful heads to contribute at a reduced strength, leading to more nuanced steering.

The paper demonstrates that PRISM-∆ significantly outperforms existing methods across various benchmarks and models, showing substantial relative gains in accuracy and consistency while reducing fluency degradation. It also scales well to long-context retrieval and is compatible with efficient attention mechanisms like FlashAttention with negligible memory overhead.
